narrative:
The model determined that you have a 59% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were the length of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and the total amount you wanted to borrow. 

Your requested duration of 48 months was more than twice as long as the average among approved applicants (19 months). This longer repayment period strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk, as the model sees extended loans as carrying higher risk of default. 

Your checking account status of less than 0 DM also worked against you. Only 12.6% of applicants in the dataset have a negative balance, making this a relatively uncommon and concerning signal that increased the likelihood of being classified as high risk.

The loan amount of 4308 DM pulled slightly in the opposite direction, modestly lowering the risk score because it was not extremely large. However, this positive influence was not enough to overcome the stronger negative effects from the loan term and account status.

To improve your chances next time, consider applying for a shorter-term loan with a smaller amount if possible, and work on bringing your checking account balance into positive territory before reapplying. These changes would directly address the main reasons for the current denial. (218 words)
